messages:
infra_oncall: heads-up — after rolling calico 3.27 to west3-gpu pool at 03:10 UTC we're seeing RDMA QP setup timeouts and high packet reordering on pod-to-pod traffic. GPU training jobs failing with 'RDMA CM: timed out' logs.

nathan: observed the same. packet loss looks small but retransmits and reordering spikes. latency between pods jumped from ~200us to 1-3ms in some AZs.

karen: is this only with host-device/rdma-enabled pods or all pods?

infra_oncall: primarily rdma-enabled pods (mellanox), but some TCP-heavy pods show increased tail latency too. non-gpu pods in same node mostly fine.

sasha: can you paste the rdma cm log and a tcpdump snippet? I want to see MSS/DF flags.

infra_oncall: pasted: ```
RDMA CM: API: rdma_connect(), ret=-ETIMEDOUT count=120
ib_rdma: qp 0x7f8c: failed to transition to RTS, timeout during handshake
```

infra_oncall: tcpdump from pod veth0 -> shows lots of packets with DF set and then ICMP frag-needed messages from host gw. snippet: ```
IP 10.10.5.23 > 10.10.6.45: Flags [DF], seq 1:1201, win 65535, length 1200
ICMP 192.168.1.1 unreachable (frag needed and DF set) mtu 9000
```

ryan: sounds like a PMTU/encapsulation size regression. calico 3.27 changed GTWY/encap header handling for VXLAN/Geneve; maybe our MTU calc is off and jumbo frames are tripping.

alex: i checked calico DaemonSet args in the rollout: --encapsulation-type=geneve, --veth-mtu=1500 set by default now, but our hosts expect 9000 for RDMA. mismatch = pmtu blackhole.

nathan: we also see rtt/reordering only on inter-AZ east-west within west3, not on single-node. suggests path through ToR that strips jumbo.

sasha: quick mitigation: enable kernel tcp_mtu_probing=1 on hosts and set net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=0? that might help TCP but RDMA CM won't adapt. we can also switch calico to host-device mode for RDMA classes so traffic bypasses VXLAN/Geneve.

karen: can we do a partial rollback for the gpu nodepool (west3-gpu) only? should avoid cluster-wide rollback.

infra_oncall: deploying rollback patch to west3-gpu canary (5 nodes) now via deploy-bot. @deploy-bot please run rollback job id 2026-03-calico-rollback on nodes label pool=gpu-west3-canary.

deploy-bot: queued rollback job 2026-03-calico-rollback -> targeting nodes with label pool=gpu-west3-canary. estimated 8m. :gear:

ryan: while rollback runs, please update scheduling to avoid preemptible jobs on affected pool — we're hitting GPU job timeouts and queued retries are incurring cost. set nodeSelector on incoming training pods to avoid west3-gpu for 2h.

infra_oncall: done — adjusted admission webhook override to steer new pods away and scaled up west2-gpu by +10 nodes to absorb load.

nathan: after rollback canary we should validate: iperf between pods, ibv_rc_pingpong for RDMA QP setup, and cilium/calico syslog for encapsulation headers. run `ip link show` and `ethtool -S` to confirm MTU/tx errors.

alex: note for runbook: add check for calico encap header size vs host MTU before upgrade, and explicit opt-out for RDMA pools (host-device). open a PR to docs repo.

infra_oncall: current status: rollback canary started, 2/5 nodes rolled, one QP fail rate dropped on those nodes. continuing. will post final once all canaries done.

karen: thanks. postmortem candidate if rollback necessary across pool — this touched customer SLAs. cc @ryan for cost impact estimate.

ryan: rough calc: 8h of retries + capacity shift -> ~$12k additional GPU spend if rollback delayed. minimizing blast radius important.

infra_oncall: final update 03:58 UTC — canary rollback succeeded, we rolled remaining 20 nodes in west3-gpu. RDMA handshake error rate returned to baseline, job backlog cleared. creating incident ticket and scheduling postmortem.

sasha: adding troubleshooting notes to incident: pmtu blackhole due to calico 3.27 encap MTU assumptions + host MTU 9000 + geneve header change -> RDMA QP setup fails. recommended: host-device for RDMA pools, preflight MTU check, and clustercanary for CNI changes on RDMA-critical pools.

infra_oncall: incident ticket created: INC-2026-0421. assigning to eng-networking for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
